public_notes.title: Organizing And Building An Evidence Record
public_notes.text: The Tribe traces modern organizing to Sugar Island meetings in the 1940s and a named organization in 1953. It describes community members assembling archival and census records to support their case. This is institutional history within much longer Anishinaabeg continuity.

public_notes.title: Recognition And A Written Constitution
public_notes.text: The Tribe dates recognition to 1972 and constitution adoption to fall 1975. Those dates concern government institutions, not the origins of a people. Its separate sovereignty explanation provides a dated account rather than a current legal determination.
